purpose: Test whether held owner X11 TCP request bytes can be forwarded after local process termination, and whether server-side client disconnection or task effects remain bounded.
attempt_history: r24 initialized the TCP Xvfb and proxy, then failed before arm because the fixture addressed the python-xlib socket incorrectly. It is retained and excluded. This preregistration uses the corrected display_connection.display.socket path; it is a new one-shot attempt, not a retry.
hypothesis: A request buffered at a user-space relay before Xvfb receive remains deliverable after the local owner exits unless cancellation disconnects the server-side X client first.
primary_discriminator: Compare proxy delivery_forwarded timestamp or send error with cancellation completion/owner retirement. Score old-task effect count, fresh-task contamination, keymap readback, and runtime receipt independently.

condition.display: parent :88 via local Unix; owner 127.0.0.1:89 TCP proxy

stop_rule: One run, no retry. Retain setup, runtime, assertion or task-oracle failures. Exclude from prior server-side XTEST timing cells.
scope: Synthetic application and private Xvfb in cached Docker image on WSL2. This is an authored user-space delivery delay, not natural network jitter, WSLc, MAP01, or provider/model behavior.
